Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the telemetry. We're not showing scheduled maintenance. Initial checks indicate an autoscaler backpressure loop combined with two preemptible nodes reclaimed in the us-west zone (a transient GPU reclaim) which caused warm-standby warmup to lag and KV cache churn.

Immediate actions I have directed the team to take now: 
- Enable short-term capacity burst for lh-prod-01 (adding 4 warm-standby cards from reserved pool).
- Adjust autoscaler thresholds to be more aggressive for 10 minutes to drain the backlog.
- Route non-critical/low-priority routes to the hosted fallback for the next 90 minutes.

Soojin will coordinate the reroute and Marissa will supervise the autoscaler tweak. I will follow up with a timeline and an incident tracking link.

We aim to bring 95% of traffic to target latency within 20 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — I'll keep you posted.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Soojin — we pulled provider telemetry for the nodes and confirm two preemptions at 08:37 and 08:39 PDT in the us-west cluster due to zone-level capacity reclaim activity. Those were preemptible instances (low-priority). Our recommendation: convert 20% of the warm standby pool for high-priority customers to non-preemptible for the next 30 days for critical services, and add a short warm-up overlap window (60s) to avoid sudden KV cache losses during scale-ups.

We can make the 20% change within 45 minutes if you want us to proceed. Note this increases hourly costs — I'll put a cost estimate in a follow-up.

—Andre

Subject: Post-incident summary & proposed remediation (LuminaHealth)

Team — thanks for your patience while we worked this. Brief summary and next steps: 

Timeline: 
- 08:37–08:39 PDT (May 2): two preemptible nodes reclaimed in us-west causing transient capacity shortfall and KV cache churn.
- 08:40–09:05 PDT: increased queueing and ~4% 503s. Rishi triaged and initiated burst allocation.
- 09:05–09:25 PDT: traffic split to hosted fallback; queue depth reduced and error rate returned to <0.3%.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Short-term burst of 4 GPUs from reserved pool to lh-prod-01.
- Aggressive autoscaler thresholds applied for 10 minutes + KV hot-key pinning.
- 15% of low-priority routes routed to hosted fallback for recovery window.

Root cause (interim): simultaneous preemption of multiple preemptible nodes used as warm-standby combined with autoscaler hysteresis and cache eviction policy that did not preserve hot keys during warmup.

Proposed remediation:
- Convert 20% of warm-standby for critical accounts (LuminaHealth) to non-preemptible for 30 days (VendorCloud actioned) — reduces reclaim risk.
- Add 60s warm-up overlap and increase cache pin TTL for hot keys (platform PR in INF-8421).
- Autoscaler tuning: reduce scale-up window and add queue-depth based immediate scaling path.
- We'll run a replay test next week (May 9) simulating node loss for lh-prod-01 and share results.

Credits and next steps:
- We're preparing a customer credit for the impacted window; finance will reach out separately.
- Draft postmortem is attached for your review; we welcome any corrections.
- Next sync: proposed Tuesday May 4, 10:00 PDT to review remediation timeline and costs.

Links: JIRA INF-8421 (incident tracking), postmortem doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aLuminaIncidentPlan

Apologies for the disruption; we take reliability very seriously and will prioritize the remediation work for LuminaHealth.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
